doc.title: Tim Ries interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, March 19, 2022

title: Volume and stage setup at stadium shows; tinnitus
summary: Ries describes the roar of 50-70 thousand people, his monitor mix, and his tinnitus.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Critics, polls and the jazz press

blocks.x: How about the intensity of those shows? The volume, the lights — I don’t have a question here I’m sort of just trying to imagine it. Because I spent some time in a very loud rock band and I’m wondering what that was like for you?

I mean it’s pretty amazing just being in a place where there’s 50, 60, 70 thousand people just the volume of the people, right? I mean so screaming and yelling and like you know the cheering and singing along, I mean that volume even without us playing is already a lot so then you combine that with an array of guitars, basses and amplifiers and all that stuff. But the good thing is that we’re spaced out quite a bit on stage, and I have my own monitor so I can have in my mix I’ll have a little keyboard, a little bit of voice, a little bit of this, so I can kind of choose what I want. But you know I’m careful but my — you

know I have tinnitus which is ringing in my ears, but I got that well before the Stones playing in big bands, you know being in front of a trumpet or trombone player right by your head. I mean that’s pretty loud already. So it’s got its volume but I luckily can hear what I want from my mix so I’m pretty okay.
